sources_considered.why: Reports the IEA's January 2024 projection of data-centre electricity demand. The IEA page itself returned HTTP 403.
Reuters report of OpenAI's CEO saying AI's energy needs require a breakthrough.
Reports the WSJ finding that a leading generative AI product lost money per user on compute.
Covers OpenAI's 2022 loss, which is outside the target period.

evidence_items.explanation: Hallucinations: high rates in leading models two months before the post.

receipt.public_excerpt: Global electricity demand from datacenters could double by 2026

evidence_items.explanation: Energy: the IEA projected data-centre demand, driven partly by AI, to grow sharply. The energy problem was growing, not being solved.

receipt.public_excerpt: an energy breakthrough is necessary for future artificial intelligence, which will consume vastly more power than people have expected

evidence_items.explanation: Energy: OpenAI's own CEO said AI's power needs could not be met without a breakthrough not yet achieved.

evidence_items.publisher: Tom's Hardware (reporting the Wall Street Journal)

receipt.public_excerpt: GitHub Copilot at $10 per month, but was losing >$20 per user per month on average in early 2023

evidence_items.explanation: Compute economics: a flagship generative AI product cost more to serve than it earned. This is based on a single anonymous source cited by the WSJ.

receipt.public_excerpt: the IEA believes that "clean" energy will be able to deliver all the additional demand between now and 2026

evidence_items.explanation: Partial counterpoint on energy. The IEA expected low-emission supply to cover new demand overall. That addresses emissions and supply, not the size of AI's energy needs.

unresolved_gaps: No audited, in-period profit-and-loss figures for generative AI providers were found. The compute-economics evidence rests on one anonymously sourced WSJ report.
'Not close to being solved' is a judgement. Later falls in inference prices fall outside the target period and were not weighed.
